newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power prices up amid cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power prices up amid cooler weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. continued to move higher Wednesday, spurred by good seasonal demand as well as higher natural gas prices, market sources said.
"Loads are very high now that the weather is turning colder," said one western trader.
Traders also cited firmer spot natural gas prices, a trend also pegged to weather conditions, as helping push power prices upward.
"As prices get up into the lower 20s there is a better correlation between gas and electricity," said one trader.
Few unplanned plant outages have been seen recently and traders said supply and demand were tightly balanced.
In addition, fish-related flow requirements as well as the normal seasonal decline in streamflows are affecting hydroelectric generation in the Northwest.
Traders noted that this year's hydroelectric resources had so far returned to a more normal range after last year's much-above-normal output.
Next-day California-Oregon border firm on-peak power was last quoted $25.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $23.00-24.00 on Tuesday.
Next-day Palo Verde power was quoted $24.00-25.00, up from $21.00-24.00.
COB for November was quoted near $23.30, while December was quoted $23.00-$23.50, compared with $23.25-23.60 on Tuesday.
November Palo Verde was last quoted at $20.25-$20.40, while December was $21.75-$22.25, down slightly from Tuesday.
